Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

I’m gonna get you! phrase

in a chasing game

also I'm gonna get you, I’m going to get you, I'm going to get you, gonna get you, I’m coming to get you

classical

Ter. Hec. 358: cōnsequar jam tē, mea māter

Cōnsequar jam tē!

I’ll catch up with you in a moment!

In Terence a son’s promise to follow his mother indoors at once; in the chasing game the same words are a playful threat, for cōnsequor is to follow someone and catch up (Lewis & Short: “to reach, overtake, come up with”). No ancient chasing call is known.

Other words

  • Jam tē prehendam! — I’ll grab you in a moment!

    also used · our formation

    Prehendō, to catch hold of (Lewis & Short: “to lay hold of, to grasp, snatch, seize, catch”), with jam and the future, as in Plautus’s Jam ego hīc erō (Men. 225).

Examples

  • Ī sōdēs intrō; cōnsequar jam tē, mea māter.

    Go on in, please; I’ll be right behind you, Mother.Ter. Hec. 358

  • Fuge! Jam tē prehendam!

    Run! I’m gonna get you!composed

See also chase, hide and seek, tickle.

SourcesLewis & Short: consequor · Lewis & Short: prehendo

Terence and Plautus from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius, loci-plautus).

No ancient chasing call is known; the alternative is ours.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
